classes.content: Seven app-only native routes return complete accessible company-scoped records/history, exact prepared proposal identities and private literal confirmation fields, complete isolated previews, separate professional decisions, and independently regenerated export artifacts including saved canonical model-data JSON/Markdown. Whole private readback refuses serialized UTF-8 envelopes over 2000000 bytes without sampling; declared export downloads refuse files over 1000000 source bytes. Model content/structuredContent contain status/count/work-reference envelopes rather than those case fields. This separation depends on installed-host app-only visibility and _meta handling, which remain unverified. There is no native merger model-context or initial/model-authoring route in this increment. Ordinary specialist Codex/Cowork work can separately read selected originals and complete case data under the existing account arrangement. No automatic anonymization, local-only processing guarantee, signing, filing, company Archive output copy or engagement completion is supplied.
classes.purpose: Inspect the existing explicitly host-bound merger case and independent export readback

security_controls.control: Each dependency checks its exact operation ID, object, version and hash. Reads, imports, writes and reports require the declared actor grant and all inherited company scopes. New cross-case evidence requires an explicit file import. These are logical helper checks, not identity authentication, encryption or OS isolation.

Only explicitly selected ordinary files within the selected company source roots can be imported; symlink paths and oversized files fail. Preserved document bytes are hash-checked on review and retrieval. Generic put cannot fabricate acquired Evidence or Artifact records.

SQLite transactions, expected-version checks and immutable-record triggers preserve revisions. Approval requires a reviewer/administrator grant and an exact unchanged target with no unresolved or stale dependencies. Generic put cannot fabricate Decision records. Confirmations are recorded assertions, not verified signatures.

Only a company-scoped administrator can bind an existing client and open engagement. Imports verify exact manifest identities and fingerprints, receipt digest and file bytes, and preserve a case-local snapshot. The helper never discovers folders or writes to the source archive. These checks do not authenticate the declared operator.

Seven app-only routes use exact trusted host tenant/operator/case/operation bindings and an existing logical CaseStore actor. The unchanged public store enforces each current company grant and every inherited scope. Complete accessible records and history are retained; prepared put/workpaper/bind_archive/import_archive requests cannot embed grants or approvals. Exact host authorization is required for new Archive identities or company source roots. Public proposals are previewed on an isolated SQLite copy; live writes require literal-field CAS, complete current preview, renewed confirmation and retained intent. Separate exact-version professional assertions require the actual reviewer grant, stated role, defined scope and expressed confirmation; names are not authenticated signatures. Combined exports remain in the merger case, contain the professional dossier and workpapers and are independently regenerated byte for byte from a retained private baseline. Live permissions and every exported history record are rechecked, so a baseline cannot restore revoked company access. Only declared export artifacts or exact preserved documents can be downloaded. No model tool, arbitrary folder discovery, grant editor, individual Archive output copy, signing, filing or engagement closure is added. Initial native intake/model authoring and installed-host acceptance remain pending. Candidate source runtime/ticket repairs are separately proposed and not applied or released. The app readback includes the saved case dossier after independent export byte verification. Reopening does not write an export or request provider/server receipts. Privacy comparison reports are excluded for this pipeline.
